# Offline-format fixtures

Real `.lic`, `.mach` and offline-proof files in the exact format the Tamga
server produces, used by `tests/integration/`.

## Why these are not generated by this repository

Every fixture here was produced by a separate generator and then **verified by
`tamga-rust`'s own verifier before being written out**. That ordering is the
point. A fixture this SDK generated and this SDK verifies proves only that the
code agrees with itself; a fixture an independent implementation accepts is
evidence of interoperability.

The generator lives in `tools/fixture-generator/` and is deliberately outside
this repository's build: it needs a Rust toolchain and a checkout of
`tamga-rust`, and neither is a dependency of the library, the tests or CI.
Nothing here needs regenerating to build or run anything.

## Regenerating

```sh
cd tools/fixture-generator
cargo run   # requires ../../../tamga-rust alongside this repository
```

The generator asserts, for each fixture, that `tamga-rust` reaches the same
verdict this SDK is expected to reach -- accepting the valid ones and
rejecting the deliberately broken ones -- and refuses to write anything out
otherwise.

## What each file is

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `ed25519_pubkey.bin` | The account's Ed25519 public key, 32 raw bytes |
| `rsa_spki.der` | The RSA-2048 public key, PKCS#1 `RSAPublicKey` DER (see the note below) |
| `ecdsa_point.bin` | The P-256 public key, 65-byte uncompressed point |
| `license_plain.lic` | `base64+ed25519+v2`, no expiry |
| `license_encrypted.lic` | `aes-256-gcm+ed25519+v2`, decryptable with the licence key |
| `license_expired.lic` | Authentic signature, signed `exp` in the past |
| `license_v1.lic` | Correct in every way except the missing `+v2` suffix |
| `license_signed_over_decoded_bytes.lic` | Signed over `enc`'s decoded bytes instead of the base64 string — the format's defining trap |
| `license_plain_wrapped.lic` | The plain file with its body wrapped at 64 columns |
| `machine_ed25519.mach` | `base64+ed25519` — **format v1, refused**; see below |
| `machine_ed25519_encrypted.mach` | `aes-256-gcm+ed25519` — **format v1, refused** |
| `machine_rsa_pkcs1.mach` | `base64+rsa-sha256` — **format v1, refused** |
| `machine_rsa_pss.mach` | `base64+rsa-pss-sha256` — **format v1, refused** |
| `machine_ecdsa.mach` | `base64+ecdsa-p256` — **format v1, refused** |
| `proof.txt` | A `v1x0.` offline proof over the tuple below |
| `proof_dataset.json` | The dataset the proof covers |
| `proof_payload.json` | The exact canonical bytes that were signed, for reference |

The proof's tuple is account `01926b3e-0000-7000-8000-0000000000aa`, machine
`01926b3e-0000-7000-8000-000000000002`, fingerprint `9f8e7d6c5b4a39281706`.
The licence key for the encrypted files is `MUP7-2TQK-7FBF-4Q6H-Y7ZR-9C3V`.

## Every machine file here is format v1

Their `alg` has no `+v2` segment, and the encrypted one packs
`nonce||ciphertext||tag` into a single base64 blob. The server emits neither
shape: it writes `<encoding>+<signing suffix>+v2`, and its encrypted payload
is `base64(nonce) "." base64(ciphertext||tag)`.

The generator produced them that way because it was written from the same
misreading of the format the verifier had — which is exactly the failure mode
the note above warns about, caught two years late. They are kept and
`tests/integration/machine_file_test.c` now asserts each one is **refused**,
which is the only thing they are still evidence of. Positive machine-file
coverage lives in `../server-machine-files/`, which this repository did not
produce and must not regenerate.

The licence files here are unaffected: they are `+v2`, and the licence file's
single-blob encrypted framing is genuinely what the server writes.

## Two findings these fixtures produced

**The RSA public key is PKCS#1 `RSAPublicKey`, not SubjectPublicKeyInfo.**
`rsa_spki.der` keeps its historical name, but its contents are
`SEQUENCE { INTEGER n, INTEGER e }` — what `aws-lc-rs`'s RSA verification API
takes, and therefore what `tamga-rust` exchanges, despite that crate's doc
comment describing it as SPKI. This SDK accepts both encodings; they are
unambiguous to tell apart.

**`tamga-rust` rejects a line-wrapped PEM body.** Its parser trims only the
ends of the body and hands the rest to a strict base64 decoder, so
`license_plain_wrapped.lic` fails there — while `tamga-swift` and
`tamga-java` strip embedded whitespace and accept it. This SDK follows the
lenient majority, and that fixture exists to pin the behaviour. It is the one
file the generator deliberately does *not* run through `tamga-rust` expecting
success.

## Private keys

None are committed. The generator mints fresh key material on every run and
keeps it only in memory; a repository that ships a private key, even a
throwaway one, trains both scanners and readers to ignore the thing they
should never ignore.
